subject: Custodian bridge & zeroize sanity check for on-prem deployment
messages:
From: Jordan Meyers <jmeyers@greenline.health>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Cc: Greenline Sec Team <secops@greenline.health>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Custodian bridge & zeroize sanity check for on-prem deployment

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. We're finalizing our internal acceptance for the private deployment (VPC + on-prem HSM) and have a few narrowly scoped questions around the "custodian bridge"/BYOK flow and emergency zeroize behavior before sign-off: 

1) BYOK custody: during initial handoff we understand Redwood will accept wrapped KEKs for tenant import. Can you confirm the operator roles that will ever see unwrapped KEKs (if any)? We need an explicit list for our internal custody policy.

2) Zeroize path: in an emergency (operator compromise), what is the guaranteed timeline and mechanism for a global zeroize? Is it an HSM administrative command, a KMS revoke + key-eviction, or physical operator-zeroize? We need exact sequence for our auditors.

3) Attestation and evidence: We'll need vendor attestation for the HSM (FIPS + manufacturer attestation) and a sample evidence artifact showing an attestation check in your deployment.

4) Rotation windows and fallback: If you perform automated rotations, what's the recommended jitter/window to avoid simultaneous tenant rotations across a region? Also, is there an automatic fallback to a stateless compatible variant if rotation fails?

5) Network isolation for operator access: we want the exact list of egress IPs and minimal L4/L7 ports required for the operator bridge and remote attestation flows.

If you can reply with a short plan and any runbook snippets (attachment is fine), we'll review and set a short call with our SecOps on Thursday.

Thanks,
Jordan
Security Engineering — Greenline Medical
-- Attachment: greenline-byo-questions.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 34KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Meyers <jmeyers@greenline.health>
Cc: Greenline Sec Team <secops@greenline.health>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Custodian bridge & zeroize sanity check for on-prem deployment

Jordan — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise plan addressing each item; I've attached a short runbook excerpt and the high-level KMS/HSM diagram.

1) BYOK custody
- Operators: only the customer-designated custodians ever see unwrapped KEKs. Redwood operator accounts are strictly limited to platform-wrapped forms. We enforce operator separation via role-based policies and proof-of-possession checks at import.
- On import we accept a wrapped KEK blob (customer wraps with their public SPK). That blob is stored cipher-text only and never unwrapped on Redwood control plane. Unwrapping only happens inside the customer HSM during the import ceremony (we provide the import API that triggers a client-side unwrap).

2) Zeroize path (emergency) — guaranteed sequence
- Trigger: customer-run SRE/CS or Redwood support can request an immediate zeroize via signed request authenticated by the customer's control plane key.
- Action sequence: 1) Redwood control plane flags tenant status -> 2) Serving nodes issue HSM admin zeroize request (HSM vendor cmd) -> 3) KMS marks all keys as revoked and deletes wrapped key blobs from object store -> 4) KV caches evicted and garbage-collected -> 5) Audit record + irreversible proof-of-zeroize (signed evidence) published to customer audit log.
- Timeline: documented SLA for emergency zeroize is "within 15 minutes" for dedicated capacity and "within 30 minutes" for hosted-private mode. SLA exceptions noted in the runbook when offline ceremony is required.

3) Attestation/evidence
- We attach an example attestation artifact (redwood-kms-overview.pdf) showing HSM attestation fields (manufacturer serial, firmware hash, PCR values) and the verification step. We also include a sample signed proof-of-zeroize snippet in the runbook.

4) Rotation windows + fallback
- Recommended: stagger rotations with a tenant-specific random jitter in a 4–12 hour window to avoid correlated rotations across zones.
- Fallback: when rotation fails we have an automatic rollback path that pins to the previous key version for up to 60 minutes and retries with exponential backoff. If rollback fails, the request can be routed to a cold fallback that uses a stateless, software-wrapped compatibility variant (with reduced throughput) until manual recovery.

5) Network isolation
- Operator bridge egress: tcp/443 only to our managed bridge IPs (listed in the attachment) and 1 additional port (tcp/5222) for the attestation tunnel when using vendor attestation channel.
- Minimal ports for on-prem HSM attestation: outbound 443 to Redwood attestation collector + outbound 123 for NTP. We recommend blocking all other egress on operator nodes.

Attachments: redwood-kms-overview.pdf (high-level attestation example), runbook-diff.txt (import + zeroize steps), network-snippet.png (egress CIDR snippet)

Next steps: I can join the Thursday SecOps call; propose Thu 2027-06-10 at 10:00 PT. If that works, I'll share a short live demo of the import ceremony and the attestation artifact check.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Security & Platform Engineering — Redwood Inference

-- Attachment: runbook-diff.txt (text/plain, 8KB)

Looping in a couple of quick clarifications from the manager side: 
- Offline ceremony: we can support an offline import ceremony for customers who require hardware-only unwraps. In that scenario the zeroize timeline must be validated because physical presence may be required — we'll call this out separately in the SLAs.
- Minimum operator access: request we standardize a short-lived SAML role for operator actions (1 hour max) and Require MFA + hardware token. Can you add the SAML role stub to the runbook before the call?
- HSM vendor attestations: Jordan, please confirm which vendor you're on (Thales/Entrust/Google Cloud HSM etc.). If it's a third-party HSM we will request a signed manufacturer attestation during onboarding.

Subject: Re: Custodian bridge & zeroize sanity check for on-prem deployment

Jordan/Karthik — operational checklist and a few gotchas below drawn from recent dry-runs. I'll attach the short playbook we use for operator eviction drills.

Operational checklist (high level):
- Preflight: confirm HSM firmware hashes and PCRs (documented in attestation artifact).
- Network: restrict operator bridge egress to the specified CIDRs; run a connectivity test using the snippet in network-snippet.png.
- Import ceremony: require dual custodians (2-of-3) for any KEK unwrap; document identity proof in the ceremony log.
- Eviction flow: 1) revoke operator SAML sessions -> 2) trigger HSM admin zeroize -> 3) revoke keys at KMS layer -> 4) push audit bundle to secure S3 -> 5) rotate service tokens and revoke service-account secrets.
- Test: run a scheduled zeroize drill in a staging tenant to validate the signed proof-of-zeroize artifact generation.

Gotchas observed: 
- Some HSMs rate-limit admin commands; if zeroize is issued repeatedly during large-scale drills the control plane can get transient failures. We recommend spacing large drills across 30-minute windows.
- If using an air-gapped HSM for import, ensure we ship the import tool container and an HSM operator keyshare procedure in advance.

Attachments: operator-eviction-play.md (markdown, 12KB)

I'll be on the Thurs call and can run the demo of a staged zeroize drill if you'd like.

— Soojin
Principal Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
